mu_name_from: MuMain loads MODEL_HELM + i from HelmMale{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 139), so file 01 is index 0, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Bronze Helm. mu.db agrees: group 7 index 0, Player/HelmMale01.bmd.
why_this_one: Martin's and Harold's +2 line, and the second of their four sets to be built. The wandering merchants stock all five Bronze pieces at +2, so five of their lines were dropped by Realm.Shelf for want of a row. See shared/Market.Wandering.
keeps_head_from:
ZzzCharacter.cpp, SetCharacterScale, and this is the first name in its condition: `c->BodyPart[BODYPART_HELM].Type == MODEL_HELM` is helm index 0, which is this one. The client then sets BODYPART_HEAD to `MODEL_BODY_HELM + c->SkinIndex` - HelmClass{SkinIndex+1}.bmd, the bare head of the wearer's own class - and draws it under the helm, where every helm outside that condition gets BODYPART_HEAD = -1 and replaces the head entirely.

The model agrees from the other side, which is the check worth having: HelmMale01 names head_02 and hide and no skin sheet at all, so there is no face inside it. The Leather Helm carries 27 triangles of skin_barbarian_01 and is not in the list; the Plate Helm carries no skin either and is also not in the list, because it is a closed great helm with nothing to show. This one is an open war mask. See HelmMale03, where the same flag was first written down.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateArmor(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)`, so slot 2 is group 7, 3 is 8 and 4 is 9.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 1, 0 - the Dark Knight alone. Twenty agility beside eighty strength, and the agility is the first this project has recorded on a piece of armour: the Leather, Bone and Plate sets all ask for none.

sheet_from: Data/Player/head_02.OZJ (64x64) and hide.jpg, from MuMain. The .bmd names head_02.jpg and hide.jpg; 62 of the 68 triangles are on the first and 6 on hide. Both sheets were already in the project - Storage01, the vault keeper, wears this set's art - and re-decoding them here produced byte-identical files, which is a free check that the extraction is the same one.
sheet_note: head_02 is an open war mask from two sides: a dark bronze brow and cheek pieces with a row of rivets along the temple and nothing across the face. Mean (103, 97, 74) at chroma 30. hide is MU capping the openings, a solid black square, as on ArmorMale10. The set is bronze and the sheets say so without ambiguity: chroma runs 30 on the helm to 70 on the legs about a warm yellow-brown mean, where the Plate set is 3 to 8 about a grey. It is still plate_steel, which is worth stating because the name reads wrong. A material here is a claim about the surface - hammered, curved, worn where it is hit - and not about the alloy; the alloy is MU's paint, and a metal's albedo is its reflectance, so a warm albedo at metallic 1.0 is a warm metal with no second material needed. brass was considered and refused: that file is cast fittings, poured rather than forged and never polished, which is a guard and a pommel cap and not a cuirass.
material_note: Three islands, all of them head_02's 62 triangles and hide's 6: the brow band and the two cheek pieces. plate_steel throughout, which is the profile's default and is also the answer. The name reads wrong on a bronze harness and the material is right: it is a claim about the surface - hammered plate, curved, with a cast grain - and the alloy is MU's paint. A metal's albedo is its reflectance, so a sheet at chroma 60 about a yellow-brown mean is a warm metal at metallic 1.0 with nothing else needed.
material_overrides_why:
plate_steel keeps its reflectance and its grain, and gives up its pull toward grey and some of its polish. The set's own note is right that plate_steel is the correct material - it is a claim about the surface, hammered and curved, and the alloy is MU's paint - and it ends on 'a metal's albedo is its reflectance, so a warm sheet at metallic 1.0 is a warm metal with nothing else needed'. That last clause is the part that was not true: plate_steel ships f0_desaturation 0.75, so a quarter of the alloy was being taken out again by the very material the note is defending.

It costs more here than anywhere. These are the highest-chroma sheets in the project - 46.9 on the helm to 90.2 on the gloves, against the Sphinx gold's 75.8 and the Scale verdigris's 29.8 - so a quarter is twenty levels of bronze. At 0.75 the set reads as pale beige and does not say bronze at all.

Roughness 0.34 -> 0.46 comes with it, because saturation and polish are one question and not two - the lesson the Sphinx set taught by going neon when only the first was moved. Swept on the assembled figure at desaturation 0.75, 0.92 and 1.0 against roughness 0.34 and 0.46: at 1.0 with the library's polish the bronze is right but the shoulder and hip carry hot glassy specular, and 0.46 keeps the warmth and calms them. Still well short of the Scale set's 0.55, which is corroded where this is polished.
